parts.title: Part 1 · The Four Walls

blocks.text: Saturday, 12:20 PM. The Courtyard ke entrance par Anika ki Sunday wedding ke liye floral arch saj chuka tha. Phool khoobsurat the, lekin arch ne raasta itna tang kar diya tha ki do guests saath nahin nikal sakte. Shreya decoration bachana chahti thi; Ankita ko kal ki bheed dikh rahi thi.

Boutique se aayi chaar college friends apni-apni duniya se kuch ghante nikaal kar yahan mili thi. Ankita phone par layout dekh rahi thi, Shivani bill check kar rahi thi, Shreya florist ko sambhal rahi thi aur Taniya volunteers ko message kar rahi thi. Bina roles baante hi chaaron samajh gayi thi ki kaun kya karega.
Shreya: Maine kitni baar bola hai, entry arch left side aayega! Kal guests yahin se enter karenge.
Taniya: Agar tum teen WhatsApp groups mein teen locations send karogi toh phool wale GPS ki madad bhi nahi kar sakte.
Shivani: Pehle agreement check kar loon. Arch shift karenge toh vendor naya bill bhejega ya included hai? Kal surprise nahi chahiye.

Taniya ne ek imaginary elderly guest ban kar tang raaste se chalne ka natak kiya. Shreya hans padi, phir usse samajh aaya ki problem sach mein hai. Ankita ne phone par naya layout bana diya; chaaron ne ek hi problem ko alag nazariye se dekha.
Ankita: Arch two feet right. Phool wahi rahenge, guests ko rasta milega, aur cable corner se safely jaayegi.
Shreya: Perfect. Tere bina main aesthetic toh sambhal leti, par log andar kaise aate woh bhool jaati.
Ankita: Tu aesthetics ke chakkar mein gate bhi decorate karke band kar degi.

Taniya ne yaad dilaya ki college festivals mein bhi Ankita unke impossible plans ko workable banati thi. Shivani ne hansi chhupaane ke liye clipboard upar kiya. Ek pal ko woh phir wahi purani college gang thi.

Mahendra Mehta ek measuring tape lekar stage ke paas aaye. Shreya ke father-in-law aur Samar ke father, sixty-six-year-old Mahendra retired civil engineer the. Society ke log unhe practical advice ke liye bulate rehte the. Unhone extension cord dekha aur turant electrician ko bulane ko kaha.
Mahendra: Shreya beta, ye wire mat bichhne dena. Kal koi gir gaya toh poora function wahin ruk jayega.
Shreya: Ji Papa. Main abhi bolti hoon. Aap khade mat rahiye, chair le lijiye.
Mahendra: Retire hua hoon, furniture nahi bana hoon. Itna chal sakta hoon.

Shreya electrician ko samjhaane chali gayi. Mahendra use ghar ki apni bahu ki tarah dekhte the; unke beech roz ki chhed-chhad thi. Lekin Ankita ne layout confirm karne ko bulaya toh woh ekdum uski taraf mud gaye.
Ankita: Uncle, ye walkway three-and-a-half feet kar doon? Stage ka side thoda adjust ho jayega.
Mahendra: Haan. Aur corners open rakhna. Tum achcha soch rahi ho.
Ankita ne thank you kaha aur sketch save karke doston ki taraf chali gayi. Mahendra ke paas ab koi measurement pending nahi tha, phir bhi woh ek pal use jaate hue dekhte rahe.

READER-ONLY — Mahendra → Ankita: Mahendra ki Ankita mein dilchaspi kab ki sirf ek achchi neighbour ke liye lagav se aage badh chuki thi. Gatherings mein woh pehle uski awaaz pehchante, phir bheed mein use dhoondhte. Aaj cable ka kaam sach mein zaroori tha, magar woh jaante the ki Ankita ne madad maangi isliye unhone apna doosra kaam side rakha. Uska bharose se 'Uncle' kehna unke mann ke is raaz ko aur uljha deta. Woh apna attraction sabse chhupate the; Ankita, Samar aur Shreya ko uski khabar nahi thi. Shreya unki apni bahu thi aur uske prati aisa koi interest nahi tha.

Mahendra ne aankh wapas cable par tikaayi aur electrician ko bula liya. Bahar se wahi trusted elder the. Ankita ko toh bas ek practical problem solve hoti dikh rahi thi; reader ab unke silence ka doosra matlab jaanta tha.

Harish Sinha, Shivani ke father-in-law aur retired banker, payment approval papers lekar aaye. Saath saal ke experience ke baad bhi woh bina agreement check kiye kisi extra charge ko haan nahi keh sakte the.
Harish: Shivani, revised budget sheet mil sakti hai? Committee ko last amount confirm karna hai.
Shivani: Haan Papa, main aapko email kar deti hoon. Yeh printed version bhi le lijiye.
Shivani ne clause point out kiya aur Harish ne calmly approve kiya. Apni bahu ke saath unki conversation hamesha simple aur professional hoti thi. Tab Shreya florist ko lekar unke saamne aa gayi.
Shreya: Harish Uncle, same arch ko sirf two feet move karna hai. Naya material nahi, extra charge nahi. Aap ready ho?
Harish: Written confirmation le aao. Phir mujhe koi objection nahi.
Shreya: Done. Main decoration bachaaungi, Shivani budget, aur aap ek baar smile kar dijiyega ki hum log agree ho gaye.
Harish ki serious expression toot gayi. Woh kuch aur poochhna chahte the—shayad boutique ka haal—magar quotation decide ho chuka tha. Khud apne bekaar sawaal par unhe ajeeb laga.

READER-ONLY — Harish → Shreya: Harish ko Shreya ki hansi, uska fearless confidence aur unse seedhi baat karne ka tareeka khaas lagne laga tha. Unke reserved nature ke saamne woh energy chhupkar unhe attract karti thi. Kuch meetings se Shreya ki entry room ka unke liye sabse noticeable moment hoti, aur uske jaane par woh khud ko thoda disappointed paate. Unhone apni feeling pehchaan li thi, magar kisi ko bataayi nahi. Shivani unki apni bahu thi, uske liye unke mann mein sirf familial respect tha. Shreya unke raaz se anjaan thi.
Vendor ne written confirmation bhej diya; extra payment nahi thi. Harish ne sheet band kar di, aur Shivani ne calculation save ki. Shreya phoolon ka naya position check karne ja chuki thi.

Welcome table par Prakash Arora, Taniya ke father-in-law aur retired principal, guest direction signs dekh rahe the. Arch shift hua toh sign ka arrow bhi badalna tha, warna guests phir purane raaste par pahunchte.
Prakash: Taniya beta, parking ke volunteers ka contact Dev se mil gaya?
Taniya: Ji Papa. Do log confirm hain. Aapko numbers bhejti hoon.

Taniya ne numbers forward kiye aur guest-poster ke font par Shreya se debate karne chali gayi. Prakash ne uske kaam ko father-in-law ke familiar pride ke saath dekha. Unki private attention ka centre woh nahi thi.
Shivani revised sketch lekar table par aayi. Arrow ab bhi old entrance dikha raha tha. Usne bina Prakash ko embarrass kiye naya sign suggest kiya.
Shivani: Prakash Uncle, main fresh sign print karwa doon? Arch move hoga toh old arrow guests ko confuse karega.
Prakash: Bilkul. Tumne theek pakda. Main naam check karte karte timing miss kar gaya.
Shivani: No problem. Main corrected copy aapke paas rakhwa dungi.

Shivani jaane lagi toh Prakash ko uski pichhli baar ki accounting deadline ki baat yaad aa gayi. Ek extra sawaal mann mein aaya, magar unhone poochha nahi. Shivani ne polite smile di aur kaam par laut gayi.

READER-ONLY — Prakash → Shivani: Prakash ki Shivani ke prati attraction nayi aur dheemi thi. Uski shaant awaaz aur bina kisi ko neecha dikhaye baat correct karne ka andaaz unhe baad mein bhi yaad rehta. Kabhi-kabhi sirf do minute ki conversation ko woh ghar jaakar bhi sochte. Khud is badlav se woh thode hairaan the. Shivani ke liye woh ek helpful elder hi the. Taniya unki apni bahu thi; uske liye unke dil mein romantic interest nahi tha.

Tabhi entrance ki taraf se kisi ki seedhi aur commanding awaaz sunayi di. Colonel Virendra Rathore aa gaye the—sixty-nine saal ke retired army officer, jo society committee mein volunteer karte the. Woh chaaron women mein se kisi ke bhi father-in-law nahi the.
Virendra: Attention, team! Main gate ki barricading galat hai. Kal gaadiyan yahan tak aa gayin toh traffic ruk jayega.
Taniya: Colonel saab, aap barricades sambhaliye. Main society WhatsApp complaints sambhal loongi.
Virendra: Tum complaint control karogi? Aadha drama toh tumhare jokes shuru karte hain.
Taniya: Bilkul. Jo problem create kar sakta hai, woh solution bhi samajhta hai.

Virendra ne ek saath chaaron ke kaam ka result dekha: Ankita ka open walkway, Shivani ka correct sign, Shreya ka balanced arch aur Taniya ke ready volunteers. Taniya ne unke military-style instructions par joke kiya; Virendra bhi hans diye.

READER-ONLY — Virendra → Ankita, Shivani, Shreya, Taniya · favourite Taniya: Virendra ko chaaron women ki taraf private attraction thi, lekin sabhi ke liye alag wajah se: Ankita ki grounded warmth, Shivani ka quiet confidence, Shreya ki energetic personality aur Taniya ka fearless humour. Abhi Taniya unki favourite thi; woh aksar unke next joke ka intezaar karte. Virendra kisi ke father-in-law nahi the. Unhone apni dilchaspi chhupaye rakhi; chaaron ke liye woh bas society ke strict-but-friendly Colonel saab the.
Virendra volunteers ko gate tak le gaye. Taniya ke liye woh bas friendly-but-strict Colonel saab the jo kisi bhi society function ko military drill bana dete the.
Arch shift hua, cable safe corner mein gayi aur naya welcome arrow lag gaya. Wedding entrance ab sirf sundar nahi tha; sachmuch usable tha. Chaaron friends ke alag skills ne ek problem solve kar di.
Shreya: Dekha? Chaaron aati hain toh problem solve ho jaati hai.
Shivani: Photo ke saath final timing bhi group mein daal dena.
Ankita: Updated layout bhi send kar rahi hoon.
Taniya: Achcha ab decide karo, kal hum guests hain ya unpaid event staff?

Anika ka voice note aaya: 'Kal guests aaram se andar aa jaayen, bas. Phool kam bhi hue toh chalega.' Shreya ne phone dekha aur dramatic saans bhari—'Bride ko kya pata humne phool bhi bacha liye aur guests bhi!' Chaaron hansi. Unke liye yeh dosti aur ek wedding ka usual din tha.

Rehearsal music bajne laga. Chaaron friends next task ki taraf chal di; unhe kisi secret ka andaaza nahi tha. Lekin reader ke liye wahi normal conversations ab alag meaning rakhti thi: ek elder ka purana pull, doosre ka self-conscious interest, teesre ki quietly developing attraction aur chauthe ki chaaron mein alag preference. Kisi woman ne attraction return nahi kiya tha, aur koi future encounter abhi establish nahi hua tha.

parts.title: Part 2 · Ankita

blocks.text: Hall ke entrance par floral arch ab theek jagah tha. Ankita ne phone par revised layout bheja hi tha ki registration desk se kisi ne kaha, 'QR scan ho raha hai, lekin list mein naam doosri baar aa raha hai.' Usne sirf ek nazar tablet par daali. Yeh decoration ka issue nahi tha; guest ke liye yahi pehla real interaction hota.

Counter sambhaal rahe event-tech vendor ne apna introduction diya: Nikhil Sethi, thirty-five, wedding ke digital check-in system ka on-site specialist. Usne screen Ankita ki taraf ki. Guest-list sync ko lekar vendor aur volunteer pichhle das minute se ek-doosre ko blame kar rahe the.
Nikhil: Data duplicate ho raha hai. Back-end list mein entry ek hi hai, lekin volunteer refresh kare toh check-in waapas pending aa jaata hai.
Ankita: Ek baar mujhe guest ban kar try karne dijiye. Aap mujhe instructions mat dijiye.

Nikhil screen se hat gaya. Ankita ne ek loose curl kaan ke peeche kiya aur tablet uthaya. Koi dramatic entry nahi thi, phir bhi uske calm andaaz ne bheed mein Nikhil ka dhyaan khinch liya. Ek pal ko usne screen ke bajay uski concentrated aankhen dekhi, phir khud ko kaam yaad dilaya.
Ankita: Technical bug baad mein fix kar lenge. Abhi problem yeh hai ki user ko success dikh nahi rahi. Volunteer ko lagta hai button nahi chala, woh dobara tap karta hai.
Nikhil: Toh success state screen par hold karni hogi. Aur button ko temporarily disable?
Ankita: Exactly. Phir ek visible 'Next Guest'. Aur internet gaya toh paper backup—kal koi queue mein khada nahi rehna chahiye.

Volunteer ne wahi flow repeat kiya. Is baar Nikhil ne temporary setting adjust ki, aur Ankita ne aakhri confirmation khud check ki. System production-ready nahi tha, lekin usko test karne aur guest ko properly guide karne ka plan ab clear tha.
Nikhil: Aap UX designer hain? Aapne bug aise pakda jaise guest ki taraf se soch rahi ho. Aur itna politely kisi ko galat prove karna bhi ek talent hai, Ankita.
Ankita: UX mein sabse buri screen woh hoti hai jo kaam kar jaaye, par user ko pata hi na chale.

Nikhil hansa. Tech group mein number add karte waqt bola, 'Kal test ke liye message kar sakta hoon?' Ankita ne aankh uthayi: 'Sirf test ke liye. Nahi toh Shreya ko forward kar doongi.' Dono muskura diye. Number ka exchange purely practical tha, lekin kuch seconds ka woh shared joke phir bhi usual vendor conversation se alag laga.

PRIVATE REACTION — Nikhil: Nikhil Ankita ki confident voice se impress tha; uski achanak aayi smile ne is appreciation ko personal bana diya. Woh jaanta tha ki Ankita married hai, aur is feeling ko professional distance ke andar rakhna chahta tha. Phir bhi uske chale jaane ke baad usne khali counter ki taraf ek baar dekha. Apni attraction ka pata usne kisi ko nahi chalne diya; Ankita toh bilkul anjaan thi.

Reception desk chhodkar Ankita clubhouse café pahunchi toh Shreya already do coffees order kar chuki thi. Hall se yahan tak aane mein bas kuch minutes lage the. Shreya ne pehle coffee, phir Ankita ki taraf aankh uthayi.
Shreya: Madam designer, ab venue ka entrance bhi tumne bachaya, tablet bhi. Wedding mein dulhan ko bulaun ya tumhara product launch karun?
Ankita: Pehle coffee de. Do ghante se sirf logon ke 'urgent' messages sun rahi hoon.

Shreya ne cup uski taraf slide kiya. College se ab tak Ankita ka yahi pattern tha: strangers ke saamne measured, apno ke saath ekdum relaxed. Shreya ko uske badalte expressions padhne ke liye kisi meeting ka summary nahi chahiye tha.
Shreya: Waise woh tech wala tumhe dekh kaise raha tha, notice kiya? Jab tum hansi na, uski troubleshooting do seconds ke liye band ho gayi.
Ankita: Tu bhi na! Usko software fix karna tha, mujhe nahi. Aur meri smile pe itna analysis mat kar, madam.
Shreya: Software mein error tha, teri smile mein nahi. College se tere saath yahi problem hai, Ankita—koi tareef kare toh seedha nazar neeche. Phir bolti hai kisi ne notice kiya hi nahi.

Ankita cup ko hothon tak le jaati-jaati ruk gayi. Shreya ke saamne woh jhooth bol bhi nahi sakti thi. Gaal ki halki garmahat chhupane ke liye usne khidki ki taraf dekha. Shreya ki aankhon mein wahi bachpan-wali shararat thi.
Shreya: Dekho, dekho! Ye blush toh shaadi ke baad bhi gaya nahi. Ritvik ko pata hai na uski biwi ko ek compliment se itna laal kiya ja sakta hai?
Ankita: Aur mujhe lagta tha boutique kholne ke baad tu mature ho jayegi. Dono predictions galat nikli.

Shreya ne hansi ke saath uska stole seedha kar diya. 'Tu itni composed banti hai,' usne chheda, 'par ek sincere tareef aate hi teri aankhen pehle answer de deti hain.' Ankita ne uska haath halka sa hata kar coffee uthayi, bina naraz hue.
Ankita: Tu meri best friend hai ya meri daily performance reviewer?
Shreya: Best friend. Reviewer hoti toh is smile ke premium charges leti.

PRIVATE REACTION — Ankita: Ankita apni looks aur competence dono se anjaan nahi thi, lekin kisi ajnabi ki nazar mein apna ek aur version dekhna use achanak conscious kar deta. Shreya shayad bas mazaak kar rahi thi. Phir bhi uske mann mein woh chhota sa sawal reh gaya: Nikhil sach mein use dekh raha tha? Usne khud ko answer dene se rok liya. Yeh sirf curiosity thi, koi naya rishta nahi.

Dono ne Sunday ke outfits aur friends group ke baare mein bhi baat ki. Shreya ne reminder diya ki kal sabko same timing follow karni hai. Ankita ke phone par 2 PM review ka calendar alert aaya. Usne coffee finish ki aur ghar ki taraf nikli; clubhouse se apartment tak ka raasta chhota tha.

1:55 PM tak Ankita apne ghar ke desk par thi. Rey drawing book lekar living room mein baitha tha; Ritvik ne headphones ki taraf ishara karke muskura diya, jaise keh raha ho, 'support ticket shuru?' Ankita ne laptop khola aur scheduled client video call join kar li.

Screen par pehle Karan Malhotra aaye, thirty-six, client-side Product Manager. Confident tone aur chhoti, friendly jokes unki habit thi. Dusri window mein Aman Joshi, thirty, front-end developer, comparatively quiet tha; woh screen share aur implementation notes dekh raha tha.
Karan: Ankita, you saved us from that onboarding screen last week. Aaj koi aur surprise hai toh first five minutes mein bata dena.
Ankita: Surprise nahi, user test hai. Aur haan—jo screen aapko clean lagti hai, zaroori nahi ki new customer ko bhi samajh aaye.
Karan: That's why I keep asking for your opinion, Ankita. Tum jab disagree karti ho toh screen par bhi lagta hai saamne baith kar keh rahi ho, 'Convince me if you can.' Difficult to ignore.

Karan ki last line par Ankita ne camera ko ek second dekha, phir screen share on kar diya. Uski awaaz bilkul steady thi, lekin baalon ke paas se ek loose strand hataate hue woh muskuraayi. Karan agle slide par tha; Ankita us chhoti si tareef ko pehle hi professional folder mein rakh dena chahti thi.
Ankita: Agar submit successful hua, toh user ko visible acknowledgement chahiye. Otherwise woh dobara tap karega. Same mistake aaj ek guest check-in tablet par dekh kar aa rahi hoon.
Aman: Wait. Is case mein blank screen animation nahi hai. API response aane tak state reset ho rahi hai. We can fix that before Monday demo.
Aman ne pehli baar lambi baat ki. Usne exact console state explain ki, aur Ankita ne uski baat bina interrupt kiye suni. Karan joking tone se serious review mode mein aa gaya.
Ankita: Good catch, Aman. Main clearer confirmation copy design kar deti hoon. Tum loading state preserve kar paoge?
Aman: Haan. Aur error message ko bhi readable bana sakte hain. Abhi woh sirf code dikha raha hai.
Karan: One designer, one developer. Main is call mein sirf coffee supply karne aaya hoon kya?
Ankita: Aap final approval de dijiye. Coffee meeting ke baad bhi chalegi.

Teenon hans diye. Karan ne decision note kiya, Aman ne patch ke liye estimate diya, aur Ankita ne screen recording mein relevant point mark kar diya. Kisi ne unnecessarily personal baat nahi badhayi; room mein professional respect aur halka sa familiar banter saath chal raha tha.
Karan: Actual device par flows test karne hain. Agar aap aaj later studio aa sakti hain, toh on-screen assumptions verify ho jayengi. Otherwise Monday tak delay hoga.
Ankita: I can leave around three. I won't promise a fix until I see the hardware. Send me the test build and location.
Aman: Build share kar deta hoon. Jo changes review mein approve hue hain unko separate list mein rakh raha hoon.

PRIVATE REACTION — Ankita: Karan ki khuli tareef aur Aman ki kam shabdon mein di gayi appreciation usse alag-alag tarah yaad rahi. Meeting khatam hote hi bhi usne ek pal ko apni screen mein reflection dekha aur khud par muskura di. Woh married thi, apne kaam aur boundaries ko jaanti thi; kisi ka aapko notice karna aur us notice ka meaning nikaalna alag cheezein hain. Teen baje wali meeting ko lekar ek halka sa anticipation reh gaya.

Call 2:35 PM ke kareeb end hui. Ankita ne notes save kiye, vendor ke check-in issue aur client review ko alag task lists mein rakha, phir kitchen ki taraf gayi. Uske paas next appointment ke liye tayyar hone ka thoda waqt tha.
Ritvik dining table par Rey ki drawing dekh raha tha. Ek chhota sa crayon rocket paper ke corner tak pahunch gaya tha. Ankita paani lene aayi toh Ritvik ne uski taraf dekha.
Ritvik: Weekend pe bhi clients ko tumhari yaad aa rahi hai? Main soch raha tha shaadi ki rehearsal ke baad hum ek ghanta relax karenge.
Ankita: Review sirf screen ka tha. Ab device test in person karna hai. Main teen baje nikalungi; zyada lamba nahi hona chahiye, but promise nahi karungi.
Ritvik: Achha. Rey aur main rocket ko Mars tak pahunchate hain. Tum wapas aakar landing approve kar dena.

Rey ne bina upar dekhe announce kiya ki rocket Mars nahi, chocolate planet jaayega. Ankita hansi. Usne Ritvik se poochha ki kal ke guest schedule ka message dekh liya hai ya nahi; usne kaha calendar already update hai.
Ritvik: Waise aaj tumhari Shreya se coffee hui? Jab tum dono milti ho toh tumhari hasi ki battery full ho jaati hai.
Ankita: Haan. Aur woh abhi bhi mujhe blush karne ka certificate baant rahi hai.
Ritvik: Reasonable. Tum boardroom se argument jeet sakti ho, lekin koi keh de 'aaj achchi lag rahi ho' toh aankhen neeche. Waise aaj achchi lag rahi ho.

Ankita ne Ritvik ko dekha aur hansi. 'Tum bhi Shreya ki team mein?' Ritvik ne cup uske haath mein diya. Saalon ka familiar, easy affection uske liye ghar jaisa tha. Bas aaj ek naye compliment ki yaad be-wajah uske khayalon mein aayi, aur usne khud ko us par hairaan paaya.
Ankita ne laptop bag mein charger, notebook aur phone rakha. Ritvik ne poochha cab chahiye ya woh gate tak drop kare. Ankita ne kaha society gate se cab mil jayegi, aur ghar ki keys check kar li.

Doorway par Ankita ne Rey ko flying kiss bheji, Ritvik ko bye kaha aur bag ka strap theek kiya. Screen par Karan ka notification aaya: 'Test build shared. See you at the review.' Usne padha, phone lock kiya aur apartment se bahar nikal gayi. Teen baje ki mulaqat abhi hui nahi thi.
Darwaaza uske peeche band ho gaya. Andar ghar ki familiar awaazen thi; bahar ek ordinary Saturday ka agla, abhi unknown chapter. Ankita meeting ke liye nikli thi—wahi Part 2 ka aakhri pal tha.

parts.title: Part 2 · Shivani

blocks.text: Hall ke floral arch ka problem solve ho chuka tha. Shivani revised guest list lekar bridal room mein aayi. Sea-green saree ka pallu neatly pinned tha, baalon ke paas chhoti pearl earrings chamak rahi thi. Woh apni appearance par kabhi shor nahi karti thi; shayad isi liye Anika ne mirror mein uska reflection dekhte hi smile kar di.
Anika: Aao Madam Sinha! Face par phir audit report wala expression? Kal meri shaadi hai, income-tax raid nahi.
Shivani: Main bas guest list dene aayi hoon. Aur in dono mein left wala dupatta better hai.
Anika: Bas? Na hug, na emotion? Itni formal friendship toh meri bank manager se bhi nahi.
Anika ne use gale laga liya. Shivani ne pehle apni file bachayi, phir hansi. Anika un kuch logon mein thi jinke saamne use words carefully choose nahi karne padte the.
Anika: Ek baat bata, ye sea-green saree kiske kehne par pehni? Tu aaj itni pretty lag rahi hai ki main bride hote hue bhi tere reflection ko dobara dekh rahi hoon.
Shivani: Kyonki file complete nahi hui toh kal tumhari reception desk par guest list ke bajaye meri photo laga dena.
Anika: Saree, earring, sab perfectly manage kar leti hai. Bas koi 'beautiful' keh de toh tu pallu ke peeche kyun chhup jaati hai?
Shivani: Bride ko free service. Baaki tumhare hone wale husband ka audit next month se chargeable hai.

Anika ki hansi par Shivani ne pallu shoulder par aur theek kar liya. Mirror mein apni halki laal hoti cheeks dekhi toh woh khud bhi hans padi. 'Tu shy hai, boring nahi,' Anika ne aankh maari. Shivani ne dheere se jawab diya, 'Aur tu bride hai, saint nahi.'
Anika: Bas! Yahi Shivani chahiye mujhe kal. Bahar Madam CA, andar chhupi hui full naughty bestie.

READER-ONLY · Shivani: Shivani ko kisi ki nazar ka ahsaas jaldi hota tha aur woh turant aur composed ban jaati. Anika jaanti thi ki uski reserved smile ke peeche kitni shararat chhupi hai. Kuch tareefon se woh embarrassed hoti thi; kuch ko chupchaap apne mann mein repeat karti. Dono baatein ek saath sach ho sakti thi.
Door par knock hua. Sahil Khurana, thirty-four, Anika ka fiancé, ring-box lekar andar aaya. Usne box Anika ko diya aur Shivani ko dekh kar friendly smile ki.
Sahil: Shivani, aaj ka colour tum par bahut khoobsurat lag raha hai. Ek pal ko laga bride ka rehearsal look tumne hi pehen liya. Aur venue ka entrance bhi beautifully manage hua.
Shivani: Thank you, Sahil. Entrance ke liye credit chaaron friends ko jaayega.
Anika: Sahil! Kal meri wedding hai, aur aaj tum mere saamne Shivani ki tareef mein itne fluent ho? Madame CA, sun rahi hai? Groom ki training abhi se shuru.
Sahil: Main toh keh raha tha wedding committee ke paas good taste hai. Bride ka final look toh kal hi reveal hoga.
Anika: Achha, bach gaye. Shivani, note kar. Shaadi se pehle hi compliment audit shuru karna padega.
Shivani: Compliment genuine ho toh accept kar lena chahiye. Nahi toh tum bhi meri tarah thank you bolkar chup ho jaogi.

Sahil event call par chala gaya. Door band hote hi Anika Shivani ke paas jhuki: 'Sach bata, achcha laga na?' Shivani ne haan ya naa nahi kaha; bas apni earring seedhi karne lagi. Anika ki shararti smile aur badi ho gayi. Usko jawab mil chuka tha.
Anika: Dekha? Sab notice karte hain. Tu hi apni tareef ko immediately discount kar deti hai.
Shivani: Discount nahi karti. Bas har achchi baat par red carpet nahi bichhaati.

Dono phir hansi. Anika ne Shivani ki earring seedhi kar di aur teasing mein kaha ki kal bhi yehi colour pehenna. Shivani ne jawab diya ki kal bride se competition nahi karegi. Is close friendship mein sharm aur mischief ek doosre ke against nahi, saath rehte the.

1:30 ke aaspaas office se message aaya. Monday ke client review ki signed working papers scan karne the, aur Shivani ke do interns office mein last reconciliation kar rahe the. Shivani ne Anika ko goodbye hug diya aur short drive par apni CA firm ke liye nikal gayi.

Saturday ko office almost khaali tha. Conference table par files, printouts aur ek laptop khula tha. Uske dono taraf Raghav aur Rishabh Kapoor baithe the—twenty-year-old twin brothers, commerce students aur pichhle chaar mahino se Shivani ke interns.

Raghav jahan baat pehle kar deta, Rishabh observation pehle karta. Pehle month ke ek difficult reconciliation mein Raghav ne overconfidence mein galat figure bheja tha, Rishabh ne discrepancy pakdi thi. Shivani ne dono ko saath bitha kar evidence se correct karwaya. Uske baad se dono ka kaam steadily improve hua. Is earned trust ki wajah se Shivani unhe apne favourite trainees kehti thi.
Raghav: Good afternoon, ma'am! Aaj toh aapko dekhkar lag raha hai weekend office mein bhi festival aa gaya. Sea-green really suits you. Looking lovely.
Shivani: Raghav, tum closing balance complete kar rahe the ya welcome speech rehearse kar rahe the?
Raghav: Closing balance bhi, ma'am. Compliment complimentary service hai.
Rishabh: Aur workbook actually complete hai. Is baar bhai ne kaam pehle kiya hai, commentary baad mein.

Shivani ko hansi aa gayi. Raghav ka familiar compliment sunte hi usne nazar ek pal neeche ki aur file table par rakhi. Rishabh ne bina comment kiye uske liye chair khinch di aur required document aage kar diya. Dono ek jaise chehre; attention dene ka andaaz bilkul alag.

READER-ONLY · Shivani: Internship ke pehle mahine mein Raghav ka 'aaj beautiful lag rahi hain' use awkward laga tha. Usne professionalism ki boundary gently samjhai; Raghav ne bhi usse respect kiya. Ab us cheerful greeting ki aadat si ho gayi thi. Kabhi Raghav chup rahta toh Shivani bina chahe sochti, 'Aaj kya hua?' Phir is chhoti si expectation par use khud sharm aa jaati. Aakhir woh unki mentor thi; attention enjoy karna kisi invitation ke barabar nahi tha.
Shivani: Chalo, friendly services bahut ho gayin. Workbook dikhao. Monday client ko incomplete figure nahi bhej sakte.
Raghav ne reconciliation tab khola. Ek vendor invoice do dates par same reference number se entered tha. Raghav ne duplicate kaha; Rishabh ne original documents side by side rakh diye.
Rishabh: Ma'am, amounts different hain. Shayad vendor ne old reference number reuse kiya hai. Maine original PDFs check kiye.
Shivani: Good catch. Raghav, vendor confirmation mark karo. Rishabh, evidence attach karna. Assumption ke basis par adjustment nahi.
Raghav: Noted. Aur agar hum aaj deadline se pehle finish kar dein toh responsible adults ka certificate milega?
Shivani: Certificate Monday 9:30 ko. Jab completed report mere desk par hogi.
Rishabh: Certificate mat dena, ma'am, frame kar lega. Aur... aaj ka colour genuinely achcha hai. Is baar main bhai se agree karta hoon.

Shivani ne Rishabh ki taraf aankh uthayi. Woh already workbook dekhne laga tha, jaise kuch personal kaha hi nahi. Raghav ko bhi apne quiet twin ki line par surprise hua. Shivani ke gaal par ek nayi si garmahat thi—yeh tareef usne expect nahi ki thi.

READER-ONLY · Rishabh: Rishabh chahta tha ki Shivani uske careful work ko notice kare, lekin aaj uski saree dekhkar ek personal compliment achanak nikal gaya. Uske mann mein attraction thi, phir bhi use yaad tha ki Shivani married hai aur uski senior mentor hai. Woh bas apni screen par laut gaya. Shivani uske private hesitation se anjaan rahi.

2:10 tak evidence scan ho gaya aur final workpaper folder ready tha. Shivani ne Raghav ki sticky-note checklist dekhi: No assumptions. Attach proof. Ask ma'am before sending. Last line ke paas usne chhota smiley bana diya tha.
Shivani: Tumne meri saari instructions fridge-magnet banane ka plan kiya hai kya?
Raghav: Abhi sirf three. Next week aur two add kar denge.
Rishabh: Fourth likh lo: unnecessary talking reduced by fifty percent.
Raghav: Impossible target, brother.

Shivani ne signed review page scan kiya aur shared folder mein rakha. Un dono ko Monday ka next step samjhaya. Raghav ne poochha Sunday wedding कैसी rahegi; Shivani ne kaha ki uska din society ke function mein busy hoga.
Raghav: Ma'am, Monday ko phir strict office mode? Aaj wala cheerful colour dobara peheniyega.
Shivani: Tum Monday report time par le aana. Mere saree colours ka audit abhi pending nahi hai.
Rishabh: Report ka promise main kar sakta hoon, ma'am. Iski commentary ka nahi.

Lift mein Shivani ko Raghav ki familiar line se zyada Rishabh ka hesitant 'main bhi agree karta hoon' yaad aa raha tha. Usne phone screen mein apna reflection dekha aur pallu theek kiya. Anika ki bold teasing, Sahil ki warm tareef aur twins ke opposite andaaz—har ek ne uski reserved smile ko alag tarah chhua tha.

READER-ONLY · Shivani: Office se nikalte hue usne Monday ka reminder save kiya. Uski zindagi wahi thi—Aditya, ghar, kaam, apni familiar routines. Lekin aaj kuch tareefein unexpected tarah yaad reh gayi thi. Woh kisi relationship ka decision nahi tha, sirf ek aisi private awareness thi jiske baare mein woh abhi kisi se baat nahi karna chahti thi.

parts.title: Part 2 · Shreya

blocks.text: Entrance arch ab theek tha aur society lawn mein shaam ki naram roshni utar rahi thi. Shreya Mehta deep maroon kurti aur chhote silver jhumkon mein stage ki taraf chali. Woh din bhar sabko instructions deti rahi thi, phir bhi uske kadam mein wahi confident rhythm thi. Use kya pata tha ki aaj koi uski planning nahi, uski awaaz notice karega.

Guitar lekar Aarav Khanna khada tha aur mixer par Neel Verma. Dono twenty-year-old college friends society ke jaane-pehchaane residents the. Aarav pichhle do saal se yahin rehta tha, Neel bhi regular community events ka hissa tha. Shreya ko unke naam, music habits aur last Diwali function ki mic problem tak yaad thi. Ye strangers nahi the.
Aarav: Shreya bhabhi! Aap aa gayin toh rehearsal bach gayi. Kal bride ki entry hai aur Neel mujhe guitar ki volume badhane nahi de raha.
Neel: Volume badha di toh singer kaun sunega? Tum apna solo alag se kar lena.
Shreya: Pehle dono ki ladai bandh. Mujhe start se music sunao. Anika ko ek soft entry chahiye, concert nahi.

Aarav ne guitar ka pehla chord chheda. Shreya timings likhne lagi, lekin familiar melody ne pen ki speed dheemi kar di. College ki ek bahut purani shaam yaad aa gayi aur woh apne aap humm karne lagi. Sur bilkul dheere nikla, phir thoda sa khul gaya. Jab usne dekha Aarav bajana band kar chuka hai, tab jaakar use ehsaas hua ki dono sun rahe the.
Aarav: Ek minute... aap ga rahi thi? Bhabhi, aapne yeh talent humse chhupaya hua tha?
Shreya: Main? Nahi, timing check kar rahi thi.
Neel: Timing toh perfect thi. Aapne kabhi music seekha hai?

Shreya ne bottle ka cap band kiya aur hansi ke saath nazar chura li. Boutique ke customers ki tareef woh aasani se handle kar leti thi; apni awaaz ke liye do familiar neighbours ka yun ruk kar dekhna usko bilkul alag laga. Aarav ki khuli smile aur Neel ki thoughtful khamoshi, dono ek second tak use conscious kar gaye.
Shreya: College mein gaati thi, bas. Ab kaam pe dhyaan do.
Aarav: Humne aapke saath itne society events kiye. Aapki awaaz itni achchi hai aur humein ab pata chal raha hai? This is unfair, Shreya bhabhi.
Shreya: Aur organiser ko pata hai tumhari practice abhi incomplete hai.
Aarav hansa. Neel ne bina kisi show ke melody ke last four beats repeat kiye aur kaha ki Anika ki entry se pehle ek small musical pause useful hoga. Shreya ne apni cue sheet par mark kiya.
Neel: Agar aap comfortable hain toh ek baar melody ke saath count kar dena. Aapki timing se light cue set kar sakte hain.
Shreya: Ek baar. Aur record karke kisi group mein mat bhejna.
Aarav: Promise. Secret rehearsal, secret singer.

Neel ne speakers thode soft kiye. Aarav ne guitar ki melody dobara chhedi. Shreya ne pehle ek breath liya, phir ek chhoti si line humm ki. Uski awaaz mein halka sa untrained warmth tha. Woh ek singer ka confident performance nahi, kisi purani yaad ka achanak lautna tha. Aarav ka haath strings par slow ho gaya; Neel ne usi pal ka pause note kiya.
Aarav: Bhabhi... seriously, aapki awaaz bahut khoobsurat hai. Humne aapko hamesha sabko manage karte dekha. Aaj pehli baar laga aap kuch apne liye kar rahi thi.
Shreya: Tum itni tareef karoge toh main kal se stage par aana hi band kar doongi. Aur haan, meri singing ke naam par kisi ko ticket mat bech dena.
Aarav: Dono mein se pehle wala. Doosre ke liye permission maangni padegi.

Shreya ne chart ki taraf dekha, lekin numbers ek second ko dhundhle se lage. Woh samajh rahi thi Aarav mazaak kar raha hai, phir bhi uska 'khoobsurat' kehne ka seedha andaaz use unexpectedly chhoo gaya. Usne apne aap ko sambhaal kar marker uthaya. Uski smile phir bhi poori tarah gayi nahi.

READER-ONLY · Aarav: Aarav Shreya ko society ki attractive, self-assured bhabhi ke roop mein pehle se notice karta tha. Par aaj usne usse stage ke shor se alag, apne aap mein khoyi dekha. Woh muskurahat aur ek pal ki jhijhak uske dimaag mein atak gayi. Uski teasing ke neeche aaj pehli baar ek zyada personal longing thi: kaash kal bhi aise hi do minute mil jaayen. Shreya uski soch se anjaan rahi.
Neel ne recording nahi banayi thi, bas mixer ki timing note ki. Woh cue sheet lekar Shreya ke paas aaya aur ek jagah half-beat pause suggest kiya.
Neel: Yahan jo silence tha, wahi sabse achcha part hai. Bride enter karegi toh lights isi point par open honi chahiye.
Shreya: Tum itni chhoti detail bhi notice kar lete ho?
Neel: Music mein kabhi-kabhi sabse important wahi hota hai jo sunai nahi deta.

Shreya ne Neel ki suggestion par pen rok diya aur uski taraf dekha. Woh hamesha kam bolta tha, lekin jab bolta toh seedha point par. Aaj usne music se zyada us chhoti si hesitation ko notice kiya jo Shreya khud bhi explain nahi kar pa rahi thi. Aarav ne mazaak mein Neel ke words ration karne ki baat kahi, par Neel bas muskuraaya.
Shreya: Good catch, Neel. Kal light ka timing tum set karna. Main yahi cue approve kar rahi hoon.

READER-ONLY · Neel: Neel ko Shreya ki personality pehle se achchi lagti thi, magar woh kabhi Aarav ki tarah openly nahi bolta. Uske liye attraction shor nahi thi; woh attention ka ek silent habit ban rahi thi. Shreya ne jab uski musical baat maan kar 'good catch' kaha, toh usse ek chhoti si khushi hui, jo usne kisi ko dikhayi nahi. Woh jaanta tha ki Shreya married hai; uski feelings uski khud ki private uljhan thi.

Halki hawa se cue sheet ka page uddne laga. Aarav ne pakad kar wapas diya, Neel ne mixer cover kiya. Shreya ne clip laga kar final time note kiya. Sunday ko bride-entry tune kis count par shuru hoga aur lights kis beat par on hongi, ab teeno ko clear tha.
Aarav: Kal final check par bhi aayengi na? Aur ek baat—agar kal woh melody aapko yaad aa gayi toh hum pretend karenge ki humne suna hi nahi.
Shreya: Kal aaoongi. Lekin sirf final sound check. Singing audition nahi.
Neel: Sunday noon tak speaker test complete kar denge. Backup instrumental pen drive mein bhi rahega.
Shreya: Perfect. Aur Aarav, guitar ki volume Neel set karega. Is par democracy suspend.
Aarav: Not fair, bhabhi. Aap dono ek team ban gaye ho.

Samar ka message aaya: hospital mein shift lambi ho gayi thi. Shreya ne 'Take care, dinner main dekh loongi' bheja, phir Mahi ke liye reminder set kiya. Phone lock karte waqt uske chehre par ghar wali familiar softness aa gayi. Thodi der pehle jo shy feeling thi, woh is ordinary family affection ke saath ajeeb tareeke se ek hi shaam mein maujood thi.

READER-ONLY · Shreya: Shreya ko apni beauty ki tareef sunne ki aadat thi, lekin music ki woh chhupi hui duniya kisi ne kab notice ki thi? Aarav ne seedhe kaha woh khoobsurat gaati hai, Neel ne bina shor uski timing ko respect diya. Dono compliments uske andar alag jagah thehar gaye. Usne unhe society ke do sweet, familiar friends hi samjha. Un dono ke mann mein kya chal raha tha, woh nahi jaanti thi—aur apni kuch pal ki jhijhak ka naam bhi usne nahi rakha.

Shreya ne dono ko thank you kaha aur lawn se ghar ki taraf chal di. Peechhe guitar par wahi melody phir chhedi gayi. Usne bina palte muskura kar ek sur apne mann mein poora kiya. Aarav ne usse jaate dekha; Neel ne speaker mute kar diya. Kal ka cue fix tha—par teeno ke liye aaj ki rehearsal sirf timing chart nahi reh gayi thi.

parts.title: Part 2 · Taniya

blocks.text: Shaam dhal rahi thi. Wedding entrance ban chuka tha, lawn mein music rehearse ho raha tha, aur clubhouse ke table par game cards ka rang-biranga dher laga tha. Taniya Arora ne darwaaza khola—maroon stole ka ek kona shoulder se phisla, jisey usne bina soch sambhaal liya. Saamne chaar familiar faces kisi great college debate ke jaise ek-doosre par bol rahe the. Sabne use dekha toh room ka mood palat gaya.
Tanya: Wonderful. Main games review karne aayi thi aur yahan college canteen ka extension mil gaya.
Laksh: Bhabhi, college canteen mein itne achche markers nahi milte.
Vihaan: Thirty-six question cards banaye hain. Categories approve kar do.
Tanya: Thirty-six? Wedding game hai, UPSC exam nahi.

Vihaan Arora, Dev ka younger cousin aur Taniya ka cousin-devar tha. Arjun Mehta, Samar ka cousin aur Shreya ka devar; Dhruv Sinha, Aditya ka cousin aur Shivani ka devar; Laksh Bansal, Ritvik ka cousin aur Ankita ka devar. Chaaron nineteen-year-old adults, ek hi college mein BBA marketing padhte aur bachpan se family functions mein milte aaye the. Har bhabhi se unki pehchaan thi; Taniya ke saath six months ki mentoring ne bond alag bana diya tha.

Vihaan naturally leader banta; Arjun har cheez mein colour aur style dhoondhta; Dhruv sabse quiet, par aksar sahi sawaal wahi poochhta; Laksh toh serious conversation ko bhi doodle bana deta. Taniya un chaaron ko naam se nahi, unke expressions se samajh leti thi. Aur chaaron ko pata tha—Taniya bhabhi unke jokes ka jawab bhi unhi ki language mein deti hai.
Arjun: Bhabhi, ek baat kahun? Aaj aapka look ekdum campaign cover jaisa hai. Honestly, hamare college fest ka poster aap hoti toh sab ruk kar dekhte.
Tanya: Toh poster improve karo. Compliment se poor product nahi bachega.
Laksh: Laksh ne haath jod diye. 'One compliment, one performance review!' Taniya hans padi. Arjun ne bhi hansi mein uski taraf dekha, lekin uske liye woh ek genuine compliment tha, sirf mazaak nahi.

Tanya khud marketing consultant thi—brands ko audience samajhne, campaign plan karne aur message ko engaging banane mein help karti thi. Kaam ki baat aate hi uski awaaz firm ho jaati, lekin in chaaron ke saath woh har instruction ko lecture nahi banne deti. Khaas kar Arjun ki tareef sun kar usne ek pal ko apna stole theek kiya, phir cards utha liye.
Tanya: Ek baat pehle clear karo. Guests ko hasana hai ya unki personal life ko stage par expose karna hai?
Dhruv: Humne private questions remove kiye. Har card pe pass option bhi rakhenge.
Tanya: Good. Jo comfortable nahi, unko reason dene ki bhi zaroorat nahi.

Ira Arora lemonade lekar andar aayi. Dev ki twenty-nine-year-old chhoti behen, Taniya ki nanad, public mein zyada nahi bolti thi. Lekin bhabhi ko chhedne ke liye uski ek nazar hi kaafi thi. Usne pehle Arjun ki khushi dekhi, phir Taniya ka carefully straightened stole, aur bina hansi roke table par tray rakhi.
Ira: Marketing class chal rahi hai ya favourite-bhabhi appreciation meeting?
Tanya: Tu meri side par hai ya inki?
Ira: Sach ki side par. Arjun ne tareef ki aur tumne uska campaign reject kar diya.

Sab hans pade. Taniya ne serious face banaye rakha, par aankhon ke kone already muskura rahe the. Yeh chaaron uske liye naye log nahi the. Family dinners, exam weeks aur project rehearsals se unke beech itni easy familiarity ban gayi thi ki awkward silence bhi kabhi-kabhi mazaak ban jaata.

READER-ONLY · Taniya: Taniya ko in chaaron ka shor pasand tha, kyunki use woh nervous boys yaad the jo pehle uske saamne practice bhi nahi kar paate the. Ab woh usse bilkul apni favourite bhabhi ki tarah argue karte. Kabhi-kabhi unki tareef use pleasantly surprise karti, lekin woh unhe family warmth aur gratitude samajh kar hans deti. Boys ke andar chalti personal feelings usse nazar nahi aati thi.

The first card asked couples to reveal an embarrassing habit of their partners. Taniya crossed out the question and wrote a new one: Tell us one small kindness your partner does that others might not know. Vihaan nodded and rewrote the category.
Vihaan: Same fun, but more positive. Yeh better hai.
Tanya: Exactly. Wedding guests audience hain, marketing leads nahi.
Arjun: Most stylish guest ka award bhi rakhein? Mere paas perfect nominee hai.
Ira: Apna naam likh diya hoga.
Arjun: Nahi. Taniya bhabhi.
Tanya: Rejected. Family loyalty is not audience research.

Chhe mahine pehle college marketing festival mein Vihaan itna nervous tha ki slides tez-tez change kar raha tha. Arjun tagline mein uljha tha, Dhruv ki research koi sun hi nahi raha tha aur Laksh jokes se gaps bhar raha tha. First mock pitch buri tarah fail hui thi. Woh shaam chaaron ne Taniya ko call kiya tha—aur woh unhe daantne ke bajay ghar bula laayi thi.

Do weekends uski dining table par unki practice hui. Taniya ne unke slides khud nahi banaye. Usne ek-ek se poochha, 'Customer ko tumhari zaroorat kyun?' Jab final presentation mein chaaron confident khade hue, sabse loud cheer Taniya ka tha. Tab se 'favourite bhabhi' unke liye sirf nickname nahi, ek purani gratitude thi.
Vihaan: Bhabhi, aapne humara first pitch bachaya tha. Kal ke games bhi aap hi rescue karogi.
Tanya: Rescue unko milti hai jo pehle khud kaam karte hain. Ab questions khatam karo.

READER-ONLY · Vihaan: Vihaan Taniya ki confident presence se us din se drawn tha jab usne sabke saamne uski mistake ko joke nahi banaya. Uski praise aur smile Vihaan ko unusual importance dene lagi thi; kabhi woh extra question sirf ek aur moment ke liye poochhta. Woh family bond ki boundary samajhta tha, isliye apni feeling kisi se share nahi karta. Taniya use improving young leader ki tarah dekhti rahi.
Dhruv checked another prompt about first impressions and suggested the option to skip if guests considered it too personal.
Dhruv: Host ko pass bolne wale se reason bhi nahi poochhna chahiye.
Tanya: Perfect. Is rule ko bold mein sabse upar rakho.
Laksh: Dhruv ka quote college noticeboard par jayega.
Dhruv: Spelling check kar lena.

Tanya ne Dhruv ki taraf dekha. Woh jab bolta tha toh zyada shabd nahi, magar har baar kisi ki comfort ke baare mein soch leta. Taniya ki smile is baar teasing nahi, genuinely warm thi. Dhruv ne notebook mein nazar jhuka li; use us expression ko thoda aur dekhne ki ichchha hui thi.

READER-ONLY · Dhruv: Dhruv Taniya ke jokes se nahi, unke peeche ki thoughtful woman se attract hota tha. Usse yaad tha kaise rehearsals mein Taniya sabse shy member se pehle poochhti thi ki woh bolna chahta bhi hai ya nahi. Taniya ki nazar mein woh ab bhi dependable young cousin tha; uski unsaid attraction ki ek bhi line room se bahar nahi nikli.
Ira appointed herself judge, Vihaan took the timer, Arjun became mock host and Laksh played a pretend guest. Before Taniya could escape, they seated her in the middle as a test participant.
Tanya: Main host hoon. Tum mujhe contestant kyun bana rahe ho?
Laksh: User testing, bhabhi. Apna product khud test karna hota hai.
Ira: I hate to admit it, but this is sound marketing logic.

Arjun: First prompt. Ek quality jo kisi mein sabse pehle notice ki ho. Main shuru karta hoon: Taniya bhabhi ki woh smile, jis se lagta hai bhale tumne galti ki ho, abhi duniya khatam nahi hui. And she never makes anyone feel small.

Arjun ka tone is baar bilkul serious tha. Taniya ka ready-made comeback ek pal ko kho gaya. Usne Arjun ko dekha, phir haste hue apni aankhen glass par le aayi. Ira ne sab notice kiya; usne turant koi comment nahi kiya.
Tanya: Unexpectedly sensible. Tumhe points milenge.
Arjun: Kabhi-kabhi real compliment bhi de sakta hoon, bhabhi.
Tanya: Bas roz ka quota mat banana.

READER-ONLY · Arjun: Arjun ko Taniya ka style pehle din se attractive lagta tha, isliye uski tareef karna uske liye easy tha. Mushkil tab hoti jab Taniya bina mazaak ke muskurati. Aaj usne uski kindness ki sincere baat ki aur us ek silent second ko yaad rakh liya. Taniya ne bas appreciate kiya; Arjun ki private feelings ka asar uski samajh mein abhi tak nahi aaya.
Laksh turned around a hand-drawn card. It showed a stern Taniya in the middle of four helpless students carrying colourful posters.
Ira: Yeh Taniya bhabhi hai ya school principal?
Laksh: Favourite bhabhi, marketing mentor and unpaid creative director.
Tanya: Unpaid? Tumhari rehearsal ki chai mein main fully compensated thi.
Laksh: Next project mein bhi chai chalegi?
Tanya: Next project mein completed assignment chahiye. Chai bonus.

Laksh ne cartoon par uski smile thodi aur badi bana di. Taniya usse hans kar daant rahi thi, aur Laksh khud bhi muskura raha tha. Room mein sabko yeh usual banter laga. Laksh ke liye, har baar use hansa lena ek chhoti personal victory ban chuki thi.

READER-ONLY · Laksh: Laksh ke jokes ka asli target kabhi award jeetna nahi tha; woh Taniya ki khulkar nikli hansi sunna chahta tha. Usne is private liking ko kabhi seriously naam nahi diya. Taniya usse ab bhi wahi mischievous younger cousin samajhti thi jiske jokes ke saath deadline bhi deni padti hai.

They shortened thirty-six cards to twelve. Dhruv finalised the rules, Vihaan checked timing, Arjun sorted colour labels and Laksh tested the timer. The wedding game now had a workable plan rather than a list of embarrassing dares.

Cards scan karne ke liye boys ko table par chhodkar Ira Taniya ko balcony mein le gayi. Neeche lawn ki lights jal rahi thi. Taniya ne thoda jhukkar railing par kohni rakhi, aur Ira ne uski taraf dekha. Bheed mein confident Taniya, do logon ke beech kabhi-kabhi bilkul narm ho jaati thi.
Ira: Tum un chaaron ke saath itni patience kaise rakhti ho?
Tanya: Mera first marketing pitch yaad hai? Team ne bina sune reject kiya tha. Main ghar aakar royi thi. Agle din main phir prepare karke gayi.
Ira: Isliye tum inko seriously leti ho, even jab woh silly behave karte hain.
Tanya: Haan. Lekin homework maaf nahi.

Ira hansi. Usse pata tha Taniya ki jokes ke peeche kuch purani disappointments bhi hain. Ira public mein quieter thi, par apni bhabhi ko samajhne ke liye use lambi conversation nahi chahiye thi. Usne Taniya ke chehre par aayi chhoti si seriousness ko bhi pehchaan liya.
Ira: Waise Arjun ne aaj tumhari smile ki jo tareef ki, us par tum sach mein ek second sharma gayi thi. Favourite bhabhi ko bhi blush karna aata hai, interesting.
Tanya: Main shock mein thi ki usne joke ke bina poora sentence bola.
Ira: Of course, bhabhi. Of course.

Tanya ne Ira ke shoulder se shoulder takraaya. 'Zyada expert mat ban,' woh hansi. Ira ki aankhon mein wahi naughtiness thi jo bahar ke chaaron boys ke paas alag-alag tareeke se thi. Bas is baar Taniya ka jawab thoda dheere aaya.

READER-ONLY · Taniya: Taniya ko 'favourite bhabhi' sunna achcha lagta tha, aur uski wajah un chaaron ki purani mehnat aur family closeness thi. blocks.text: Dopahar ka sound-check khatam hua toh Shreya seedhe boutique pahunchi. Plum boat-neck kurti, silver jhumkas aur half-tied hair mein woh din bhar kaam sambhaal rahi thi. Neel ka headset adjust karna aur Aarav ka guitar lesson kabhi-kabhi be-wajah yaad aa jaata, toh woh khud par hans padti.
“Madam, packing rolls aa gaye,” assistant ne kaha.
Saath mein Chotu bhi tha—brown-paper rolls, tape aur garment covers lekar.
“Arre, Chotu Babu! Aaj bhi express delivery?”
“Didi, aapka boutique hi sabse zyada express demand karta hai.”
“Good. Toh tumhe award dena padega.”
“Chocolate chalegi.”
“Woh toh Mahi ke liye laate ho. Apne liye kya loge?”
“Bas ek din late delivery par daant mat dena.”
Shreya zor se hans di. “Impossible promise.”
Assistant next counter par customer ki fitting lene chali gayi. Shreya ne Chotu se ek fabric roll pass karne ko kaha. Upar wale rack mein jagah banane ke liye woh step-stool par khadi hui.

🟨 Kurti ka hem thoda sa upar utha. Side-waist ka smooth stretch clear dikh gaya. kurti ke lower edge ke upar ki skin, soft under-bust curve ki beginning — halki si, lekin visible. Jab woh aur thoda stretch hui, boat-neck se soft cleavage line bhi thodi si open ho gayi.
🟨 Chotu ne roll upar karne ke liye nazar uthayi. Ek pal ko uska haath ruka, phir usne roll theek jagah par diya.

🟨 Uske pehle Ankita ki neckline, Shivani ka upper back, Taniya ka navel — sab dekh chuka tha. Phir bhi is baar freeze hua. Alag angle tha. Side-waist ki line, under-bust ki soft curve, uski saans ka halka sa rise.
“Chotu? Roll pakde raho,” Shreya ne kaha.
“Ji, didi.”
🟨 Neeche utarte waqt Shreya ko side par hawa ka halka ehsaas hua. Usne kurti ka hem neeche kiya aur Chotu ki khamoshi notice ki.
🟨 “Kya hua? Bill bhool gaye ya boutique ka fashion sense samajh nahi aaya?”
Chotu sharmaakar hasa. “Aapke saamne kaun fashion discuss karega, didi?”
“Achha, ye toh smart answer tha.”
“Waise aaj earrings aur hairstyle bahut suit kar rahe hain.”
“Thank you! Tum toh Aarav se competition kar rahe ho aaj.”
“Aarav kaun?”
“Ek guitarist. Bahut bolta hai—tumse bhi zyada.”

🟨 Un dono ne phir normal billing ki baat ki. Shreya jaanti thi ki ab woh aasani se logon ka awkward silence pakad leti hai. Magar woh Chotu ki taraf waise attracted nahi hui jaise use sound-check par apne aap ko Neel aur Aarav ke kareeb mehsoos karke surprise hua tha. Yahaan use zyada curious amusement thi—aur ek halki jhijhak.
🟨 Aur uske body ne bhi notice kiya tha — side-waist ke around halki si warmth, under-bust mein soft awareness. Kurti ke neeche skin thodi si sensitive feel ho rahi thi.
🟨 Woh amusement ke saath self-conscious ho gayi thi. Aarav ya Neel jaisa nahi. Alag. Curious. Thoda awkward. Lekin present.
Chotu ne kaam complete kiya. Nikalte waqt uski nazar ek baar phir uske face pe gayi — controlled — phir door band ho gaya.
Shreya ne shelf ki taraf dekha.
Uske side-waist pe ab bhi us nazar ka residual feel tha.
🟨 Woh hasi toh, lekin hasi ke baad jo quiet heat bachi thi, woh gayi nahi.

🟨 Shaam ko ghar pahunchkar Shreya ne kapde badalne ke liye wash area khola. **Black lace bra** hanger par thi, lekin uski position pehle jaisi nahi thi. Usne apni aadat ke mutabik dono straps ek hi direction mein rakhe the; ab ek palta hua tha.
“Main hi jaldi mein rakh gayi houngi,” usne socha, aur hanger seedha kar diya.
Reader ko yaad tha: **Harish** ne pehle ghar ke private wash area mein bina permission woh garment uthaya tha aur awaaz aane par wapas rakha tha. Shreya ko uska pata nahi tha.
Mahi ki awaaz aayi—“Mumma, song sunao!”
Shreya muskurakar bahar aayi. Guitar ki ek galat chord aur kisi ka playful compliment phir yaad aa gaya. Woh melody gungunaane lagi.

parts.title: Part 5 · Shreya — Sunday, 6:30 PM · Boutique (second visit)

blocks.text: *Sunday · 6:30 PM · Shreya's Boutique*
Shaam tak Shreya thak chuki thi. Dopahar Neel ke saath sound-check aur Aarav se guitar seekhne waala chhota lesson ab bhi uske dimaag mein ghoom raha tha.
Ghar se boutique lautkar woh fabric rolls arrange kar rahi thi. Dopahar ko Chotu ke saamne oonchi shelf se roll nikaalte samay kurti thoda upar khisakne waala awkward moment bhi yaad aaya.
“Madam, aaj kaafi busy lag rahi hain.”
Darwaaze se Chotu ki awaaz aayi. Woh packaging ka bacha samaan lene aaya tha.
“Busy nahi, Chotu. Exhausted.”
“Phir bhi aap sab manage kar leti ho.”
“Bas, ab tum bhi compliments shuru mat karna!”
Chotu hans pada.
Shreya ne ek gift hamper nikaala.
“Achha, tumhari madad chahiye. Ye ribbon pakdo.”
Chotu ne ribbon pakda. Shreya ne use decorative knot banaana sikhaya.
“Dekho, is corner ko fold karna hai. Zyada tight nahi.”
“Didi, mere se toh grocery bag hi theek pack hote hain.”
“Practice karo. Boutique assistant bana dungi.”
Dono hanse.
Chotu ki nazar Shreya ke haathon ki tez aur saaf movements par gayi. Use yaad aaya ki yeh wahi Shreya thi jo wedding hall mein har volunteer ko bina ghabraaye nirdesh deti thi.
🟨 “Waise didi, aaj aapne gaana bhi gaya tha?”
🟨 Shreya ruk gayi. “Tumne suna?”
🟨 “Thoda sa. Bahut achcha tha.”
Is baar Shreya sachmuch muskura di.
🟨 Neel aur Aarav ne bhi uski awaaz ki tareef ki thi. Lekin Chotu se aisi baat sunne ki use ummeed nahi thi.
“Thank you, Chotu.”
“Phir kab gaaogi?”
“Pehle guitar seekh loon!”
“Guitar bhi?”
Shreya hanste hue boli, “Haan. Mere talents ki list abhi complete nahi hui.”
🟨 Woh nikalne laga. Door pe ruk kar usne ek baar peeche dekha. Shreya bhi usse dekh rahi thi. Koi extra word nahi hua.
Bas ek clear, quiet shift —
usne usse design ki tarah nahi,
body ke saath notice kiya tha,
🟨 aur usne bhi us nazar ko apne body pe feel kiya tha.
Shreya ne door band kiya.
Kurti ke neeche uski skin ab bhi thodi si aware thi.
Amusement ab bhi tha.
🟨 Lekin uske neeche ek chhoti si unfinished heat bhi thi.
Woh Aarav-Neel wali attraction nahi thi.
Yeh alag thi.
Nayi.
Residual.

Chotu ne receipts band kar di. Usse kisi ghar ke **missing ya displaced private garments** ke baare mein kuch nahi pata tha. Woh sirf apni deliveries jaanta tha; chaaron auraton ke alag andarooni sawaal nahi.
Aur chaaron gharon mein, din ki normal routines ke beech, ek-ek chhota sawaal bina jawab ke reh gaya.

parts.title: Part 5 · Taniya — Monday, 11:00 AM · Clubhouse Cleanup

blocks.text: *Monday · 11 AM · Clubhouse Cleanup*
Wedding event khatam ho chuka tha, lekin clubhouse mein abhi bhi samaan ke boxes rakhe the.
Taniya ne clipboard uthaya.
“Vihaan, Arjun, Dhruv, Laksh! Tum chaaron kal wedding games ke heroes the. Aaj cleanup se bhaag kyun rahe ho?”
Laksh ne naatkiya andaaz mein haath jod diye.
“Bhabhi, heroes ko recovery day milna chahiye.”
“Achha? Toh recovery ke paise bhi kaat loon?”
Sab hans pade.
Tabhi Chotu khaali cartons lene aaya.
“Good morning, Taniya didi.”
“Arey Chotu! Tum aa gaye. At least ek responsible ladka toh hai yahan.”
Arjun ne turant kaha, “Bhabhi, hum chaaron ki insult ho rahi hai!”
Taniya hansi. “Insult nahi, performance evaluation.”
Chotu ne bade cartons uthaane shuru kiye. Taniya ek table ke paas khadi hokar use labels bata rahi thi.
Kal ki storeroom ghatna ke baad woh saavdhaani se chal rahi thi. Laksh ne bhi yaad dilaya:
🟨 “Bhabhi, floor par koi kapda ho toh pehle mujhe bula lena.”
“Bilkul nahi! Tumhari rescue service ki rating bahut kharaab hai.”
Sab phir hans pade.
Chotu kuch der chupchaap kaam karta raha.
🟨 Taniya ne poochha, “Kya hua? Tum bhi inke jokes se darr gaye?”
🟨 “Nahi didi. Bas aap kal se itna kaam kar rahi ho. Thakti nahi?”
Taniya ek pal ko ruki.
“Thakti hoon, Chotu. Bas in chaaron ke saamne admit nahi karti.”
Vihaan ne uski taraf dekha. “Bhabhi, hum help toh kar rahe hain.”
“Kar rahe ho. Lekin supervision ke bina tum chaaron ka result doubtful hai.”
🟨 Arjun ne mazaak mein kaha, “Chotu ko fifth devar bana lo. Team strong ho jayegi.”
Laksh turant bola, “Nahi bhai, phir favourite bhabhi ka favourite devar competition badh jayega.”
Taniya ne clipboard band kar diya.
“Bas! Ab jo sabse pehle boxes finish karega, usko chai milegi.”
“Bhabhi, sabko!” Laksh chillaaya.
“Dekhenge!”

🟨 Chotu ek carton uthane ke liye jhuka. Taniya usi line mein labels chipka rahi thi. Jab woh thoda aage badhi, unka distance kam ho gaya. Uske blouse ka side uske arm ke near se guzra. Touch nahi hua. Bas nearness.
🟨 Chotu ne thoda sa step back liya. Taniya ne notice kiya.
Kal wala moment dono ke beech ab bhi tha.
Kaam ke beech mein Taniya ne usse clipboard diya. “Yahan count likh do.”
🟨 Uske haath ne clipboard pakda. Unki ungliyan ek second ke liye close aayi. Chotu ne eyes upar uthaye. Taniya bhi usse dekh rahi thi.
Koi extra word nahi hua.
🟨 Bas ek chhota sa, clear register — kal usne uska navel dekha tha, aur aaj dono us baat ko jaante the bina bole.
🟨 Taniya ne pallu set kiya. Uske andar kal wala residual warmth phir se uth gaya. Bahut halka. Control mein. Lekin present.
Chotu ne count likh diya aur doosre carton ki taraf chala gaya. Uske shoulders thode set the.
Taniya ne uske peeche dekha.
Part 4 ka fall ab bhi body mein tha.
Kal ki nazar ab bhi mind mein thi.
🟨 Woh ab jaan ti thi ki yeh tension sirf uske dimaag mein nahi thi.
Chotu bhi carry kar raha tha.
Cleanup continue hua.
Bahar se normal.
Andar, ek quiet, unfinished awareness.

parts.title: Part 6 · ANKITA — MONDAY, 4:10 PM · BANSAL APARTMENT

blocks.text: Ankita ne laptop band kiya toh screen par uska hi reflection reh gaya. Lunch ke baad se woh laundry service ke teen emails padh chuki thi. Teesra email bhi pehle do jaisa tha: *We are investigating your complaint.*
“Investigating,” usne dheere se dohraya. “Kapde missing hain, koi murder mystery nahi.”
Phone ka screen chamka. Chirag ka message tha: *Didi, app wala form submit ho gaya. Ek verification code ka doubt hai. Kal aa sakta hoon?*

Ankita ne turant reply type kiya—*Haan, screenshot bhej do.* Phir ungli ruk gayi. Kal saamne baithkar uska form samjhate waqt Chotu kitna dhyaan se sun raha tha. Aur usse ek din pehle, Rey ke rocket ke paas, baat karte-karte achanak chup kyun ho gaya tha?
Woh baat usne kisi se nahi kahi thi. Ritvik se bhi nahi. Isliye nahi ki koi bada raaz tha; bas isliye ki woh khud use ek naam nahi de pa rahi thi.

Almirah se kapde nikaalte waqt uski nazar soft blue sleeveless cotton kurti par padi. Summer mein woh ise ghar par pehenti thi. Pichhle kuch dino se usne zyada tar workwear hi pehna tha—tailored trousers, fitted tops aur woh cream stole jo har meeting mein sambhalna padta.
Usne kurti pehni, baal ek loose knot mein bandhe aur mirror ke saamne ruki. Neckline uski usual office kurti se thodi khuli thi; kapda halka tha, lekin comfortable. Woh apne aap ko dekhkar hansi.
“Ankita Bansal. Client calls mein five stakeholders sambhal leti ho. Ek delivery boy ki awkward silence analyse nahi kar paa rahi?”
Mirror ne jawaab nahi diya.
Phone par usne likha, *Kal 4 baje aana. Rey school se late aayega, aaraam se form dekh lenge.*
Send karne ke baad use khayal aaya ki usne “aaraam se” kyun likha. Form sach mein dekhna tha; yeh bhi sach tha ki woh Chotu ka pehle wala surprise dobara samajhna chahti thi.

**READER-ONLY — ANKITA:** Usne outfit sirf uske liye khareeda nahi tha, lekin aaj use chunne mein Chotu ki nazar ki yaad zaroor shamil thi. Yeh faisla uska apna tha. Use koi idea nahi tha ki Chotu kal ko uski kis baat par react karega.
Ritvik ka call aaya. “Evening ko jaldi aa paunga. Rey ke science project ka kya hua?”
“Scientist ne launch postpone kiya hai,” Ankita ne jawab diya. “Aur haan, laundry complaint abhi pending hai.”
“Main follow up kar deta hoon.”
“Nahi, main kar lungi.”
Usne phone rakha aur apne reflection ko ek baar phir dekha. Abki baar usne smile chhupaayi nahi.

parts.title: Part 6 · SHIVANI — MONDAY, 6:35 PM · SINHA APARTMENT

blocks.text: Shivani ke saamne Monday ka audit workbook khula tha, magar uski nazar baar-baar phone par chale jaati. Raghav aur Rishabh ka report-review theek raha tha. Kaam ke waqt kisi ne Saturday ki uncomfortable bike ride ka zikr nahi kiya. Dono poore din numbers aur proofs ki baat karte rahe.

Woh wardrobe ke paas gayi. Sea-green saree ab neatly folded thi. Uske bagal mein ek cream saree aur matching blouse rakha tha—back par dori baandhne wala, jise woh festivals mein pehenti thi. Shivani ne blouse uthaya. Back ka design kaafi khula tha, lekin front properly fastened tha. Usne use mirror ke saamne hold kiya. Hair bun karne par kandhon ke beech ki skin nazar aati. Pehle woh sochti thi ki us outfit par Aditya kya kahega. Aaj usse ek aur naam yaad aaya—Chotu.
Usne khud se poochha, *“Agar woh dekhe toh? Kya main itni sharmilaungi jitna kal hui thi?”*
Isi sawaal se use sabse zyada ghabrahat hui.

Woh Chotu ko ek mehnati, decent ladka samajhti thi. Kal breakfast par jab usne padhaai ki baat ki thi, Shivani uske liye genuinely khush hui thi. Aaj pehli baar woh notice kar rahi thi ki uski apni curiosity bhi is connection mein aa gayi hai. Yeh baat use achchi bhi lagi aur ajeeb bhi.
Aditya room mein aaya. “Woh blouse phir se? Tumhe yaad hai na iski dori pehle loose thi?”
“Haan. Tailor ko dena hai.”

Shivani ne aankh uthayi. “Main sambhaal lungi.”

Woh chala gaya. Shivani ne blouse ko alag hanger par rakha.

**READER-ONLY — SHIVANI:** Chotu ka kal aana sirf ek practical errand tha. Shivani ka kal usi blouse ko pehenne ka faisla practical nahi tha. Woh dekhna chahti thi ki kya ek shant, formal Shivani ke alawa koi doosri Shivani bhi uski aankhon mein dikh sakti hai. Dori ki kamzori ya usse hone wali awkwardness ka usne koi plan nahi banaya tha.
Usne khidki band ki aur kitabein sametne lagi. Excitement ke saath ek sankoch bhi tha. Woh kisi baat ka jawaab abhi nahi chahti thi.

parts.title: Part 6 · TANIYA — TUESDAY, 12:40 PM · ARORA APARTMENT

blocks.text: Taniya ne wedding-game photos ki memory card laptop mein lagayi. Har dusri photo mein kisi na kisi ka face funny tha. Ek photo mein Laksh ka haath hawaa mein tha aur Arjun aankhein band karke speech de raha tha.

Dev office gaya tha. Ira ne subah call karke poochha tha ki final albums kab milenge. Taniya ne vaada kiya tha ki shaam tak shortlist bhej degi.
Chotu ka message aaya: *Didi, remaining decor sheets lene 2 baje aa jaaun?*

Side angle se fabric uske hips ka silhouette follow kar raha tha.
Taniya ne khud ko dekhkar muskuraya. “Theek hai, madam. Marketing ka first rule: presentation.”

Usko Chotu ka Sunday wala nervous glance yaad aaya. Phir Monday clubhouse mein Laksh ka joke—*fifth devar competition*. Us waqt usne usse sirf hasi mein uda diya tha. Aaj pata nahi kyun, woh dono moments uske saath chale aaye.

Usne ek photograph kholi jisme woh camera ki taraf dekhkar hans rahi thi. Phir doosri, jo side profile thi.

Ira ka phone aaya.

Phone rakhkar woh ek pal ke liye chup hui. Usne Chotu ke saath akele photo opinion lene ka plan khud banaya tha. Is baat ne use thoda surprise kiya.

**READER-ONLY — TANIYA:** Usne outfits aur photographs khud select kiye. Woh apne look ke baare mein Chotu ka honest response chahti thi—aur shayad uski famous teasing ko kisi naye insaan par aazmaana bhi. Lekin reaction ka control uske haath mein nahi tha.

parts.title: Part 6 · CLOSING INTERCUT — CHIRAG

blocks.text: Society store mein Chirag ne delivery screen kholi. Chaar addresses alag time slots mein the; uske liye ab bhi yeh kaam tha, koi secret itinerary nahi.

parts.title: Part 7 · Shreya

blocks.text: Boutique ki front window se subah ki light aa rahi thi. Assistant ne backdrop seedha kiya, phir reception ki taraf chali gayi — customer call.

Shreya shoot corner ke paas khadi thi. Wine-coloured saree, fitted blouse, V-shaped neckline. Mirror ke saamne chuni hui **second pallu placement** abhi bhi wahi thi. Tuesday 9:20 par woh changing-room se bahar aa chuki thi aur Chotu ko extra assignment bol chuki thi. Ab usi baat ko aage badhana tha. Doosra look usne honest opinion ke liye chuna tha, sirf camera ke liye nahi.

Chotu counter pe khada tha. Chirag. Saal bhar se Mehta boutique ki deliveries karta tha. Familiar face, natural halki teasing. Aaj Tuesday, 9:25. Woh receipt aur backdrop stand ke kaam se aaya tha. Shreya didi ne shoot corner mein hi kaha tha ki usse photograph aur honest opinion bhi chahiye.
“Chotu Babu, jo extra assignment bola tha, ab uska practical bhi ho jaaye?”
Woh muskuraaya. “Overtime milega, didi?”
“Ek chocolate. Aur ek honest opinion. Galat diya toh photo dobara.”
Usne apna phone uske haath mein diya, camera khola, floor pe chalk mark dikhaya.
“Yahan se frame. Colour natural aana chahiye.”
